description: Per-character dash tuning: maximum and regenerating dash gauge, up-front and sustained gauge costs, minimum/cancel timings, two-stage S-M-E speed curves with steering and lean, air-dash gravity, homing-dash motion, and animation-rigidity classes. Five exported shards feed one manager array; character, shikigami and character-specific controllers select rows.

Id.simple: Row key used to select this dash tuning row.
Id.technical: Unreal DataTable row name (exported as ID). ResolveDataRows searches ActionDashDataTables with ActionDataTable.Id_ActionDash after StudioBattleCharacterOverrides.ActionDashIdOverride and stores the first hit in AGameCharacter.ActionDashRow; a miss fails character setup. Shikigamis resolve their own row with ShikigamiDataTable.Id_ActionDash (a miss fails their setup too). Helper finders also request hard-coded keys: CP_210_2 cached during CP_210 sheathed-row setup and returned while bWeaponDrawn == 1, CP_180_ATTACKG_1/2/3 for the second beam hit, and CP_240_ATTACKG_<level> during CursedEnergyAttack_1/Air_1.

Gauge.technical: Gauge points. UpdateDashGauge selects this value when Setup.SoloSide != 1, then multiplies by GetDashGaugeMaxRate (battle-team rate, equipment and binding-vow DashGaugeMax effects, and a HitPoint-ratio effect). The result seeds DashGauge at setup, revive and round/battle resets. Exports span -1 to 800, including zeroed specialized rows and several NPC rows at -1; the reconstructed consumer has no special case for negative or zero values.

Gauge_Solo.simple: Maximum dash gauge for a solo-side setup.
Gauge_Solo.technical: Used in place of Gauge only when Setup.SoloSide == 1, the one-member-side flag assigned by battle-phase setup (the shared BattleFree_PairSoloSide table is used by several phases; Aging Online has its own table); it is also passed through GetDashGaugeMaxRate. Most exported rows match Gauge, but CN_081 and CN_150 export 1200 versus 600 in Gauge.

GaugeRecoverWaitTime.simple: Delay before dash gauge starts regenerating.
GaugeRecoverWaitTime.technical: Seconds. SetDashGaugeRecovering(true) copies this into the DashGaugeRecoverWait countdown and stops the active interpolation; dash Start disables recovery and NormalDashEnd Start re-enables it, while many other action hooks toggle the same flag. While recovery is enabled and no DashGaugeNotRecoverItem buff is present, the countdown is reduced by GetActionValue100() * DeltaTime. Exports span -1 to 1.0, with ordinary character rows clustered around 0.3-0.6; the field is used directly as a seconds countdown rather than a gauge cost.

GaugeRecover.technical: After the wait expires, Speed = GetDashGaugeRecoverRate() * this field; a nonpositive result is forced to 1.0, then an interpolation from 0 to GetDashGaugeMax() runs for 100 / Speed and its per-tick delta is added to DashGauge. Exports are -1, 0, 450, 500 or 600; nonpositive results are clamped to 1.0 after the rate multiplication, and the 100 / Speed divisor is explicit in the reconstructed code.

Dash_GaugeConsumeBegin.simple: Up-front gauge cost of starting a grounded dash.
Dash_GaugeConsumeBegin.technical: Gauge points, charged once when NormalDashBegin starts. Cost = GetDashGaugeConsumeRate(NormalDashBegin) * this field, where that rate combines the battle ally rate, status/equipment/binding-vow effects and the action's chase-versus-escape rate; bDashGaugeUnlimited forces the cost to zero. Taking the cost also clears the recovery wait and stops interpolation. Exported values range from 0 to 200.

DashAir_GaugeConsumeBegin.simple: Up-front cost of an air dash; also reused as a CP_180 timing gate.
DashAir_GaugeConsumeBegin.technical: Gauge points in ConsumeDashGaugeBegin for NormalDashAirBegin, with the same rate and unlimited-gauge handling as Dash_GaugeConsumeBegin. CP_180 overloads it for its selected ATTACKG row: StartAttackHoming immediately starts the homing dash on the second CursedEnergyAttack_1 hit, then TickAttack uses this field as an elapsed-time threshold in seconds to end that follow-up (apply homing inertia and the passive buff, restore the camera and clear aim/action flags). The specialized CP_180_ATTACKG_* exports use 0.45 here (a time gate), whereas ordinary rows export 0-300 (gauge points); the overloaded units are explicit in the consumers.

NormalDash_Minimum_Time.technical: Seconds. NormalDash::GetMinimumTime returns GetDashMinimumTimeRate() * this field (CP_180 uses the same formula). The dash loop multiplies that result by the owner run-speed rate; only after elapsed time exceeds it can low gauge or released dash input end the dash. Exports span 0-0.5, with ordinary character rows mostly 0.3-0.4.

NormalDash_CancelInput_Time.technical: Seconds multiplied by the owner run-speed rate. NormalDash::UpdateRequests appends queued action requests only after Elapsed reaches that threshold, regardless of whether the dash itself continues; CP_180 overrides UpdateRequests with the same calculation.

NormalDash_GaugeConsume.technical: Gauge points per second. After the consume delay elapses, each dash-loop tick calls ConsumeDashGauge(DeltaTime, NormalDash), which deducts GetNormalDashGaugeConsumeRate() * this field * DeltaTime and clamps at zero. That rate includes the battle ally rate, status effects from the forward-versus-camera chase/escape test, equipment/binding vows and the action rate; bDashGaugeUnlimited zeroes it. Exported values span 0-300.

NormalDash_GaugeConsume_DelayTime.simple: Grace period before grounded dash gauge drain.
NormalDash_GaugeConsume_DelayTime.technical: Seconds. NormalDash::Start stores this as GaugeConsumeDelayTime unless the previous action was NormalDashAir, in which case it inherits the previous loop's remaining delay (previous delay minus previous Elapsed) and sets bFromDashAir. The loop compares the stored delay with Elapsed before charging NormalDash_GaugeConsume. CP_180 has a matching getter.

NormalDash_Turn_DelayTime.simple: Steering lockout at the start of a grounded dash.
NormalDash_Turn_DelayTime.technical: Seconds. SetMoveMode copies it into DashTurnDelay for move modes 6, 8, 9, 10 and 30. TickMovement decrements the delay each step; only at zero does input steering update anim-instance lean and call TurnYawToward with NormalDash_Rotation_Speed. Landing mode 12 deliberately preserves the remaining delay.

NormalDash_Speed_S.simple: Starting speed of the grounded dash speed curve.
NormalDash_Speed_S.technical: Table speed value used as the From of a FloatInterp28 S-to-M curve with EaseOut. Applied by SetMoveMode cases 6, 8, 9, 10 and 30 and by shikigami move modes 2/20. Exports span 0-6000, including zeroed specialized rows.

NormalDash_Speed_M.simple: Middle speed of the grounded dash speed curve.
NormalDash_Speed_M.technical: First interpolation target from NormalDash_Speed_S over NormalDash_InterpolateTime_M, then the From of the second M-to-E curve when the first curve ends. The landing mode 12 curve instead starts from the current speed and targets min(NormalDash_Speed_E, current). Shikigami dash modes use the same S/M split.

NormalDash_InterpolateTime_M.simple: Duration of the S-to-M grounded speed blend.
NormalDash_InterpolateTime_M.technical: Seconds passed as the duration of FloatInterp28.Start when a grounded dash move mode starts; shikigami modes 2/20 use it for the same S-to-M blend. The M-to-E blend uses NormalDash_InterpolateTime_E instead.

NormalDash_Blend_Exp_M.simple: Easing exponent for the S-to-M grounded speed blend.
NormalDash_Blend_Exp_M.technical: Passed to FFloatEaseInterpolator.Start together with EaseOut when the S-to-M curve begins; shikigami mode 2/20 uses it identically. It is a shape parameter, not a duration. Exported ordinary rows mostly use 1.0.

NormalDash_Speed_E.simple: Final speed of the grounded dash speed curve.
NormalDash_Speed_E.technical: Target of the M-to-E curve started once the initial S-to-M interpolation is inactive. In landing mode 12 the target is min(this value, current speed) instead. Shikigami dash modes also use it as their M-to-E endpoint.

NormalDash_InterpolateTime_E.simple: Duration of the M-to-E grounded speed blend.
NormalDash_InterpolateTime_E.technical: Seconds. Used for the second speed interpolation on normal, target and landing dash modes (6/8/9/10/12/30) and for the shikigami dash M-to-E curve; it is not the minimum dash time.

NormalDash_Blend_Exp_E.simple: Easing exponent for the M-to-E grounded speed blend.
NormalDash_Blend_Exp_E.technical: Exponent argument of FloatInterp28.Start with EaseOut for the M-to-E curve; shared by character landing/target dash modes and shikigami dash mode 2/4.

NormalDash_Rotation_Speed.technical: Rate passed to TurnYawToward after NormalDash_Turn_DelayTime has expired when there is nonzero input. Used by the normal dash, alternate normal-dash tick, target-dash tick and shikigami ground-dash mode 2. Shikigami follow-dash mode 20 instead uses NormalDashAir_Rotation_Speed; zero removes steering rather than shortening the delay.

NormalDash_Inertia_Rate.simple: Inertia carry-over rate after a grounded dash.
NormalDash_Inertia_Rate.technical: Passed as the rate to SetInertia when the previous action is NormalDash and to BlendInertia from FGameCharacterAction::BlendInertiaFromAction; shikigami ApplyPrevInertia uses the same pair for the Dash action type. Specialized controllers also stop their motion and apply it when leaving a dash-like phase: CN_140 phase 3 and CP_240 AttackG phase 2. Rate is a multiplier on the remaining motion, paired with NormalDash_Inertia_Time. CN_060 uses the air counterpart for its airborne transitions.

NormalDash_Inertia_Time.simple: Inertia carry-over duration after a grounded dash.
NormalDash_Inertia_Time.technical: Duration paired with NormalDash_Inertia_Rate in SetInertia/BlendInertia when a NormalDash action ends or is blended out; also applied by CN_140, CP_240 and shikigami Dash actions at their dash-motion stop points. Exports span 0-2.5, with ordinary rows often 0.5-0.8.

NormalDash_Lean_Rate.technical: Passed to UpdateLeanRate for the anim instance's left/right lean during grounded-dash steering, once NormalDash_Turn_DelayTime has elapsed; the landing and target dash ticks repeat the same call. Shikigami follow/dash and attack-motion ticks use this field for both LR and UD lean, so it also affects shikigami body roll.

NormalDash_Lean_Max.technical: Cap paired with NormalDash_Lean_Rate in UpdateLeanRate on the same grounded steering, landing and target-dash paths. Shikigami follow-dash, attack-approach and attack-motion steps also pass it for both LR and UD lean.

NormalDashAir_Minimum_Time.technical: Seconds. NormalDashAir::GetMinimumTime multiplies this field by GetDashMinimumTimeRate(); the shared dash-loop check then multiplies by the owner's run-speed rate before deciding whether low gauge or released input may end the dash.

NormalDashAir_CancelInput_Time.technical: Seconds multiplied by the owner run-speed rate. NormalDashAir::UpdateRequests appends queued requests only after Elapsed passes this threshold; bFlag14 can instead request an immediate landing dash.

NormalDashAir_GaugeConsume.technical: Gauge points per second. The dash loop deducts GetDashAirGaugeConsumeRate() * this field * DeltaTime through ConsumeDashGauge after NormalDashAir_GaugeConsume_DelayTime; the rate includes the battle ally rate, status/equipment effects and the forward-versus-camera chase/escape multiplier, and unlimited gauge zeroes it.

NormalDashAir_GaugeConsume_DelayTime.simple: Grace period before normal air-dash gauge drain.
NormalDashAir_GaugeConsume_DelayTime.technical: Seconds. NormalDashAir::GetGaugeConsumeDelayTime exposes it to the shared dash loop. A NormalDash started directly from NormalDashAir inherits the air dash's remaining delay (air dash delay minus air dash Elapsed) rather than reading the grounded delay.

NormalDashAir_Turn_DelayTime.simple: Steering lockout at the start of a normal air dash.
NormalDashAir_Turn_DelayTime.technical: Seconds. SetMoveMode case 7 copies it into DashTurnDelay; TickModeNormalDashAir decrements it each step and only steers toward input after it reaches zero. Turning then uses NormalDashAir_Rotation_Speed.

NormalDashAir_Speed_S.simple: Starting speed of the normal air-dash speed curve.
NormalDashAir_Speed_S.technical: From value of the S-to-M interpolation when move mode 7 or shikigami air-dash mode 3 starts. Exported values are character-specific and can be higher than the M speed, producing a deceleration into the middle phase.

NormalDashAir_Speed_M.simple: Middle speed of the normal air-dash speed curve.
NormalDashAir_Speed_M.technical: First interpolation target from NormalDashAir_Speed_S, then the From of the M-to-E curve after the first curve finishes. Used by character mode 7, shikigami air dash mode 3 and shikigami follow-dash mode 20.

NormalDashAir_InterpolateTime_M.simple: Duration of the S-to-M normal air-dash speed blend.
NormalDashAir_InterpolateTime_M.technical: Seconds passed to FloatInterp28.Start when character mode 7 or shikigami mode 3 begins. The later M-to-E transition uses NormalDashAir_InterpolateTime_E.

NormalDashAir_Blend_Exp_M.simple: Easing exponent for the S-to-M normal air-dash speed blend.
NormalDashAir_Blend_Exp_M.technical: Exponent passed with EaseOut to the S-to-M FloatInterp28 on character mode 7 / shikigami mode 3. It controls curve shape only; exported air-dash rows commonly use 2.0.

NormalDashAir_Speed_E.simple: Final speed of the normal air-dash speed curve.
NormalDashAir_Speed_E.technical: Endpoint of the M-to-E air-dash curve started when the S-to-M interpolation becomes inactive; used in character mode 7, shikigami mode 3 and shikigami follow-dash mode 20.

NormalDashAir_InterpolateTime_E.simple: Duration of the M-to-E normal air-dash speed blend.
NormalDashAir_InterpolateTime_E.technical: Seconds used for the second speed interpolation in character mode 7, shikigami mode 3 and shikigami follow-dash mode 20. It is independent of the gravity delay and minimum dash time.

NormalDashAir_Blend_Exp_E.simple: Easing exponent for the M-to-E normal air-dash speed blend.
NormalDashAir_Blend_Exp_E.technical: Exponent passed with EaseOut to the M-to-E FloatInterp28 on the same character and shikigami air-dash tick paths. Exported rows commonly use 2.0.

NormalDashAir_Rotation_Speed.technical: Rate passed to TurnYawToward after NormalDashAir_Turn_DelayTime expires in character mode 7. Shikigami follow-dash mode 20 and shikigami air-dash mode 3 use this same field (not NormalDash_Rotation_Speed for the air follow turn) when steering toward their follow direction.

NormalDashAir_Inertia_Rate.simple: Inertia carry-over rate after a normal air dash.
NormalDashAir_Inertia_Rate.technical: Passed to SetInertia/BlendInertia when the previous action is NormalDashAir; shikigami ApplyPrevInertia uses the same pair for DashAir. CN_060 also applies it when an action leaves the ground and again when it reaches its final phase; a wall-hit branch returns before that second call, so this field affects more than the air-dash End action.

NormalDashAir_Inertia_Time.simple: Inertia carry-over duration after a normal air dash.
NormalDashAir_Inertia_Time.technical: Duration paired with NormalDashAir_Inertia_Rate in SetInertia/BlendInertia for a previous NormalDashAir action, in the CN_060 airborne action transitions and in shikigami DashAir actions. Exports span 0-2.0, with many rows at 0.9.

NormalDashAir_Gravity.simple: Gravity used by the normal air-dash fall curve.
NormalDashAir_Gravity.technical: Passed as the gravity argument to BuildFallCurve(0, value, Global.DashAirFall_Speed_Max) when character mode 7 or shikigami mode 3 starts; the resulting curve is sampled for vertical speed once the gravity delay expires. A zero value produces no downward acceleration from this curve.

NormalDashAir_Gravity_Delay_Time.technical: Seconds. SetMoveMode/set shikigami mode stores it in AirDashGravityDelay; each character mode 7 / shikigami mode 3 air-dash tick decrements that countdown and only samples its dash-air fall curve once it reaches zero. The landing reset of MovePhaseElapsed seen in TickModeNormalDash(bAir=true) belongs to the separate mode 9 jump-derived fall curve, not to this AirDashGravityDelay countdown. Exported ordinary rows mostly use 0.

HomingDashAir_GaugeConsumeBegin.simple: Up-front gauge cost of a homing/auto-attack air dash.
HomingDashAir_GaugeConsumeBegin.technical: Gauge points charged once for HomingDashAirBegin and AutoAttackDashAirBegin. The cost uses GetDashGaugeConsumeRate(Type), including the input-direction chase/escape rate, and is forced to zero by bDashGaugeUnlimited. Exported values vary by row; many rows use 0.

HomingDashAir_Minimum_Time.technical: Seconds. HomingDashAir::GetMinimumTime multiplies it by GetDashMinimumTimeRate(); HomingDashAir::IsDashContinuing then multiplies by the run-speed rate and keeps the dash active while the warp target is ahead and that threshold has not yet passed. Once it has passed, continuation depends on remaining dash gauge (not held dash input); AutoAttackDashAir inherits this check.

HomingDashAir_CancelInput_Time.technical: Seconds multiplied by the owner run-speed rate. HomingDashAir::UpdateRequests and the AutoAttackDashAir override both wait until Elapsed reaches this value before appending queued action requests; this does not by itself end the dash.

HomingDashAir_GaugeConsume.technical: Gauge points per second. After HomingDashAir_GaugeConsume_DelayTime, each tick of HomingDashAir or AutoAttackDashAir deducts GetDashAirGaugeConsumeRate() * this field * DeltaTime from the gauge; unlimited gauge overrides it to zero.

HomingDashAir_GaugeConsume_DelayTime.simple: Grace period before homing air-dash gauge drain.
HomingDashAir_GaugeConsume_DelayTime.technical: Seconds returned by HomingDashAir::GetGaugeConsumeDelayTime to the shared dash loop. Until Elapsed exceeds it, no HomingDashAir_GaugeConsume is charged. AutoAttackDashAir inherits the same getter.

HomingDashAir_Speed_S.simple: Starting speed of the homing air-dash speed curve.
HomingDashAir_Speed_S.technical: From value of the S-to-M curve. StartHomingDashAir receives an explicit row (CP_180 can pass its ATTACKG dash row) and caches it as DashRow450; SetMoveMode case 11 instead reads the current owner dash row. Both paths start with this speed and EaseOut.

HomingDashAir_Speed_M.simple: Middle speed of the homing air-dash speed curve.
HomingDashAir_Speed_M.technical: First interpolation target from HomingDashAir_Speed_S at StartHomingDashAir or SetMoveMode 11. When that curve finishes, the homing tick restarts a M-to-E curve from this value using DashRow450 when cached, otherwise the current owner dash row.

HomingDashAir_InterpolateTime_M.simple: Duration of the S-to-M homing air-dash speed blend.
HomingDashAir_InterpolateTime_M.technical: Seconds passed to FloatInterp28.Start for the S-to-M curve at StartHomingDashAir and move mode 11. The second M-to-E transition uses HomingDashAir_InterpolateTime_E.

HomingDashAir_Blend_Exp_M.simple: Easing exponent for the S-to-M homing air-dash speed blend.
HomingDashAir_Blend_Exp_M.technical: Exponent supplied with EaseOut when the homing dash S-to-M interpolation starts from either StartHomingDashAir or SetMoveMode 11. Exported rows commonly use 2.0.

HomingDashAir_Speed_E.simple: Final speed of the homing air-dash speed curve.
HomingDashAir_Speed_E.technical: Target of the M-to-E curve started when the first homing speed interpolation completes. The row used for this phase is the cached DashRow450 when StartHomingDashAir supplied one, else the current owner dash row.

HomingDashAir_InterpolateTime_E.simple: Duration of the M-to-E homing air-dash speed blend.
HomingDashAir_InterpolateTime_E.technical: Seconds used for the second homing speed interpolation in TickModeHomingDashAir. It is distinct from the homing cancel/minimum times and from NormalDashAir_InterpolateTime_E.

HomingDashAir_Blend_Exp_E.simple: Easing exponent for the M-to-E homing air-dash speed blend.
HomingDashAir_Blend_Exp_E.technical: Exponent passed with EaseOut to the homing M-to-E FloatInterp28 on the same cached-or-current row used for HomingDashAir_Speed_E.

HomingDashAir_Rotation_Speed.simple: Homing air-dash yaw rate toward the warp point.
HomingDashAir_Rotation_Speed.technical: Rate passed to TurnYawToward in TickModeHomingDashAir when bSteerTowardMoveInput is set, turning the owner toward the normalized direction to DashAirWarpLocation. Unlike grounded dash steering, this path does not check a turn-delay field. Every exported row sets this field to 0, so no homing yaw rotation is observed in the cooked data; the travel direction is then fixed by the warp point.

HomingDashAir_Inertia_Rate.simple: Inertia carry-over rate after a homing air dash.
HomingDashAir_Inertia_Rate.technical: Rate used by SetInertia/BlendInertia when the previous action is HomingDashAir. CP_180 also applies it after the DashAir_GaugeConsumeBegin elapsed-time gate in the second beam attack, using the attack-specific dash row it selected.

HomingDashAir_Inertia_Time.simple: Inertia carry-over duration after a homing air dash.
HomingDashAir_Inertia_Time.technical: Duration paired with HomingDashAir_Inertia_Rate for a previous HomingDashAir action and for CP_180's post-gate beam-dash inertia transition. Exports span 0.5-2.0.

Rigidity_DashBegin.simple: Rigidity class for grounded dash startup.
Rigidity_DashBegin.technical: EGameActionRigidityType value converted to a zero-based index into GlobalCorrect.Rigidity_DashBegin; the fetched rate (default 1.0) multiplies the action controller's dash-begin play rate to scale the begin animation. CP_010 passive buffs can further adjust the rate. Constructor default is None; exports use Light/Normal/Heavy.

Rigidity_DashEnd.simple: Rigidity class for grounded dash ending.
Rigidity_DashEnd.technical: Indexed into GlobalCorrect.Rigidity_DashEnd; the resulting rate scales GetDashEndPlayRate for the end animation, with CP_010 and CP_240 passive buffs modifying the rate. Default is None in the reconstructed row constructor.

Rigidity_DashAirBegin.technical: Indexed into GlobalCorrect.Rigidity_DashAirBegin; the rate scales GetDashAirBeginPlayRate (which reuses the action controller's dash-begin rate slot) for the air-dash begin animation, with CP_010 passive adjustment. Default is None.

Rigidity_DashAirEnd.technical: Indexed into GlobalCorrect.Rigidity_DashAirEnd; the fetched rate scales GetDashAirEndPlayRate (the action controller's dash-end rate slot), with CP_010 and CP_240 passive adjustments. Default is None.

notes: Five assets (ActionDashDataTable1-5) are loaded into AGameDataTableManager.ActionDashDataTables in that order; character, shikigami and CP_180 finders return the first table containing the requested key. Export keys are unique across the five shards (57 rows total).

Pointer aliasing matters: AGameCharacter stores ActionDashRow from ResolveDataRows, GetCurrentActionDashRow prefers the action controller's GetActionDashRow when a controller exists, and CP_210/CP_240 override that virtual. CP_210 caches CP_210_2 when rows are initialized and returns it only while bWeaponDrawn == 1. CP_180 passes an explicit ATTACKG row into StartHomingDashAir; that row is cached as DashRow450 for the homing speed phase and is also read by CP_180's beam gate/inertia path, while gauge/status code still uses the owner's current row. CP_240 returns nullptr rather than the owner row while its attack condition is active if the named ATTACKG row is missing.

Speed groups follow a two-stage FloatInterp28 curve: S to M when the move mode starts, then M to E when that interpolation becomes inactive. Landing mode 12 starts from current speed to min(Speed_E, current). Shikigami movement modes 2/3/20 consume the same NormalDash* fields from their own DashRow.

DashAir_GaugeConsumeBegin is overloaded: it is a one-time gauge cost for NormalDashAirBegin, but CP_180_ATTACKG_* rows export 0.45 and CP_180 uses that value as an elapsed-time gate in seconds to terminate the second beam attack's homing follow-up (applying HomingDashAir inertia, buff and camera/flag changes).

Gauge, Gauge_Solo and the *_GaugeConsume* fields are gauge points; *_Time and *_DelayTime fields are seconds in the traced code; speed fields are table speed values consumed directly by movement interpolation; Rotation_Speed is a yaw rate. Multipliers from battle settings, equipment, binding vows, buffs and action-controller slots can change the applied cost, maximum, play rate or minimum time.

Exported data observations include Gauge = -1 on CN_010, CN_020, CN_040, CN_220 and CN_231, Gauge_Solo = 1200 versus Gauge = 600 on CN_081/CN_150, zeroed Gauge and speed fields on CP_180_ATTACKG_*, and CP_210_2 as a distinct row requested by CP_210. No special case for -1 appears in the reconstructed consumers.

The reconstructed row constructor initializes every float to 0 and every Rigidity_* field to EGameActionRigidityType::None; all 57 exported rows serialize every catalogued field, so exported values are cooked table data, not constructor defaults.

All findings come from the locally reconstructed C++ and static export/loader evidence. No launch, network access or retail verification was used, so retail-faithful behavior outside these traced paths remains unproven.

usages.detail: Loads the five exported shards into ActionDashDataTables; names are registered at lines 380-384.
ResolveDataRows find the required row by ActionDataTable.Id_ActionDash or the studio ActionDashIdOverride and store AGameCharacter.ActionDashRow.
GetCurrentActionDashRow returns the stored row when no action controller exists, otherwise the controller's virtual row.
Shikigami setup resolves its own dash row from ShikigamiDataTable.Id_ActionDash and stores it as AGameShikigami.DashRow.

CP_180_FindActionDashRow walks the manager array; the second CursedEnergyAttack_1 hit uses CP_180_ATTACKG_<level>, passes it to StartHomingDashAir immediately, then uses the same row's DashAir_GaugeConsumeBegin as a 0.45 s end-gate before applying HomingDashAir inertia.
Caches CP_210_2 and returns it from GetActionDashRow while bWeaponDrawn == 1.
Returns CP_240_ATTACKG_<CursedEnergyLevel> while CursedEnergyAttack_1/Air_1 is the active attack layer; otherwise falls back to the owner row.
Shared dash loop applies delay-gated per-tick gauge drain, minimum time and dash-input continuation.
Ground dash captures its gauge-consume delay, inheriting the remaining delay when started from an air dash.
Action exit and blend paths apply the NormalDash/NormalDashAir/HomingDashAir inertia rate and time by previous action type.
SetMoveMode initializes S-to-M speed curves and turn/gravity delays for ground, air, homing and dash-jump modes.
Tick modes start M-to-E curves and feed lean and yaw turn settings from the current dash row.
StartHomingDashAir accepts an explicit row and caches it as DashRow450 for the homing speed phase.
Shikigami follow-dash mode reuses NormalDashAir speed, lean and rotation fields from its own DashRow.
Shikigami ground/air dash modes reuse NormalDash and NormalDashAir speed and lean curves.
UpdateDashGauge selects Gauge or Gauge_Solo, applies the maximum-rate multiplier and resets the gauge.
SetDashGaugeRecovering seeds the GaugeRecoverWaitTime countdown and stops interpolation.
ConsumeDashGaugeBegin charges the three dash-begin costs with rate multipliers and unlimited-gauge override.
ConsumeDashGauge drains sustained dash costs per tick by action type.
After the wait, GaugeRecover drives a 0-to-max interpolation over 100 / Speed.
Rigidity enums are mapped through GlobalCorrect arrays to dash/air-dash begin and end animation play rates.
Beam follow-up uses DashAir_GaugeConsumeBegin as an elapsed-time gate, then HomingDashAir inertia fields.
CN_060 applies NormalDashAir inertia when leaving the ground or finishing its air phase.
CN_140 applies NormalDash inertia at its dash-stop phase.
Reconstructed row constructor zeroes every float and sets the four rigidity enums to None; the 57 exported rows supply cooked values.
Shikigami ApplyPrevInertia applies the row's NormalDash/NormalDashAir inertia rate and time for Dash/DashAir previous action types.
